questions.question: What is Multi-Factor Authentication (MFA)?

options.text: Authentication requiring two or more verification methods

explanation.correct: MFA requires both something you know (password) and something you have (one-time code from device) to access your account.
explanation.why: A describes a different tool. C and D are security concepts but not MFA. MFA specifically combines multiple authentication factors.

questions.question: Which of the following is NOT a type of MFA device supported by AWS?

explanation.correct: AWS supports Virtual MFA, Hardware tokens, and Security Keys, but not biometric authentication like fingerprint scanners for MFA.
explanation.why: Options A, B, and D are all valid MFA device types in AWS. Fingerprint authentication is not currently supported as an MFA method.

questions.question: How often do Virtual MFA codes (like Google Authenticator) change?

explanation.correct: Virtual MFA uses TOTP (Time-based One-Time Password) which generates new 6-digit codes every 30 seconds.
explanation.why: This 30-second interval balances security with usability - short enough to limit exposure, long enough for users to enter the code.

questions.question: Why does AWS require TWO consecutive MFA codes during device setup?

options.text: To verify the device is synchronized with AWS servers

explanation.correct: Two consecutive codes verify that your authenticator app's clock is properly synchronized with AWS time servers, preventing login issues.
explanation.why: If times are off-sync, codes won't match. By requiring two codes 30 seconds apart, AWS confirms synchronization is working correctly.

questions.question: What is the PRIMARY purpose of AWS Budget Alerts?

options.text: To automatically stop services when budget is exceeded
To notify you when spending crosses defined thresholds
To reduce your AWS bill automatically

explanation.correct: Budget Alerts send notifications when actual or forecasted costs exceed thresholds you set - they don't automatically take action.
explanation.why: AWS Budgets is notification-only. It doesn't stop services (A), reduce bills (C), or track logins (D). You must manually respond to alerts.

questions.question: What spending threshold triggers a Zero Spend Budget alert?

explanation.correct: Zero Spend Budget alerts when spending exceeds $0.01 - designed for Free Tier users who want to stay at zero cost.
explanation.why: $0.00 wouldn't be practical as the threshold. $0.01 is the minimum detectable charge and triggers immediate notification.

questions.question: Which budget type is BEST for students using AWS Free Tier?

explanation.correct: Zero Spend Budget is specifically designed for Free Tier users - it alerts immediately if any charges occur beyond free limits.
explanation.why: Free Tier should have $0 costs. Zero Spend catches accidental charges instantly. Other budgets are for paid usage scenarios.

questions.question: How many AWS Budgets can you create for free?

explanation.correct: AWS provides the first 2 budgets free. After that, each additional budget costs $0.02 per day ($0.60/month).
explanation.why: This free tier allows essential monitoring (e.g., Zero Spend + Monthly Cost) without charges for basic accounts.

questions.question: Which MFA app allows cloud backup and multi-device sync?

explanation.correct: Authy offers cloud backup and multi-device synchronization, allowing recovery if you lose your primary device.
explanation.why: Google Authenticator doesn't have cloud backup. Authy is specifically designed with backup features for this use case.

questions.question: Which AWS account should ALWAYS have MFA enabled?

explanation.correct: The Root user has unlimited access to all account resources and billing - MFA on Root is the highest security priority.
explanation.why: Root user compromise is catastrophic. While MFA on IAM users is good practice, Root MFA is absolutely mandatory.

questions.question: What are the two types of costs that AWS Budgets can track?

explanation.correct: AWS Budgets tracks Actual costs (what you've already spent) and Forecasted costs (what AWS predicts you'll spend by month-end).
explanation.why: 'Actual and Forecasted' are the official AWS terms. Forecasted uses your spending pattern to predict end-of-month totals.

questions.question: What does TOTP stand for in the context of Virtual MFA?

explanation.correct: TOTP (Time-based One-Time Password) is the protocol that generates 6-digit codes changing every 30 seconds based on current time.
explanation.why: TOTP is the industry-standard protocol used by Google Authenticator, Authy, and other MFA apps for time-synchronized codes.

questions.question: If you set a monthly budget of $50 with an 80% alert threshold, at what dollar amount will you receive an alert?

explanation.correct: 80% of $50 is $40. The alert triggers when actual or forecasted spending reaches $40.
explanation.why: Budget thresholds are percentages of your total budget. 80% × $50 = $40. This gives you warning before hitting the limit.

questions.question: Which of the following statements about MFA is TRUE?

options.text: MFA codes work indefinitely once generated
MFA completely eliminates all security risks
Even if password is stolen, account stays protected with MFA
MFA is only needed for production accounts

explanation.correct: MFA's key benefit is that password theft alone cannot compromise the account - attackers also need your physical device.
explanation.why: A is false (codes expire in 30 sec). B is false (MFA reduces but doesn't eliminate all risk). D is false (all accounts benefit from MFA).

questions.question: What happens if you lose your phone with Google Authenticator and don't have backup codes?

options.text: You can still log in with just password
You must contact AWS Support for recovery

explanation.correct: Without backup codes or alternative MFA device, you must contact AWS Support with identity verification to regain access.
explanation.why: This is why saving backup codes is critical. AWS Support can help but requires proof of account ownership.

questions.question: Which budget alert type would you use to monitor EC2 running hours instead of costs?

explanation.correct: Usage Budgets track service usage metrics like EC2 hours, S3 storage GB, or Lambda invocations instead of dollar amounts.
explanation.why: When you want to monitor resource consumption rather than costs, Usage Budgets are the right choice.

questions.question: What is the difference between 'Actual Cost' and 'Forecasted Cost' budget alerts?

options.text: Actual tracks spending so far; Forecasted predicts end-of-month total
Actual is daily; Forecasted is monthly
Forecasted is less accurate than Actual

explanation.correct: Actual Cost shows what you've spent to date. Forecasted Cost uses your spending pattern to predict the month-end total.
explanation.why: Forecasted alerts give early warning - if you're on track to exceed budget by month-end, you get alerted NOW instead of later.

questions.question: Why is Virtual MFA (authenticator app) more secure than SMS-based two-factor authentication?

options.text: SMS can be intercepted via SIM swapping or network attacks

explanation.correct: SMS-based 2FA is vulnerable to SIM swapping attacks where attackers transfer your number. Virtual MFA is device-based and more secure.
explanation.why: SMS interception is a known attack vector. Virtual MFA generates codes locally on your device without SMS transmission.

questions.question: If you create 5 AWS Budgets, what will be your monthly cost?

explanation.correct: First 2 budgets free. Budgets 3-5 cost $0.02/day each. 3 paid budgets × $0.02 × 30 days = $1.80/month.
explanation.why: AWS charges $0.02 per day ($0.60/month) for each budget after the first two. 3 × $0.60 = $1.80.

questions.question: What is the recommended best practice for MFA on IAM users?

options.text: MFA is optional for IAM users

explanation.correct: AWS recommends MFA for Root and all IAM users with administrative or privileged access to resources.
explanation.why: Admin users can launch expensive resources or access sensitive data. Read-only users may not need MFA, but admins absolutely do.

questions.question: You receive a budget alert that forecasted cost will exceed your $100 monthly limit. It's only day 10 of the month. What does this mean?

options.text: Based on current spending rate, you'll exceed $100 by month-end
You need to increase your budget

explanation.correct: Forecasted alerts analyze your spending pattern. If you've spent $30 in 10 days, AWS predicts you'll spend $90 by day 30 - triggering an early alert.
explanation.why: This early warning allows you to take action NOW (stop resources, optimize) before actually exceeding the budget.

questions.question: What protocol do Security Keys (like YubiKey) use for AWS MFA?

explanation.correct: Security Keys use U2F (Universal 2nd Factor) or FIDO (Fast Identity Online) protocols for hardware-based authentication.
explanation.why: U2F/FIDO is a phishing-resistant protocol designed specifically for physical security keys like YubiKey.

questions.question: Which scenario would benefit MOST from multiple budget alert thresholds (50%, 80%, 100%)?

options.text: Production company account with variable workloads

explanation.correct: Production accounts with variable spending benefit from graduated alerts - early warnings at 50%, action needed at 80%, critical at 100%.
explanation.why: Free Tier/learning accounts work fine with single Zero Spend alert. Production needs multiple checkpoints for cost management.

questions.question: What is the main security advantage of Hardware MFA tokens over Virtual MFA?

options.text: They're physically separate from your computer/phone

explanation.correct: Hardware tokens are air-gapped - separate from devices that could be compromised by malware. If your computer is hacked, the token remains secure.
explanation.why: Physical separation prevents malware from stealing MFA codes. Virtual MFA on a phone could theoretically be compromised if phone is hacked.

questions.question: You set a $20 monthly budget. On day 15, you've spent $8. AWS sends a forecasted cost alert. Why?

options.text: AWS predicts you'll spend more than $20 by month-end based on current trend
Budget alerts always trigger at mid-month

explanation.correct: AWS analyzes your spending velocity. $8 in 15 days = ~$0.53/day. Projected to 30 days = ~$16. But if spending accelerates, forecast could exceed $20.
explanation.why: Forecasted alerts use machine learning to detect spending patterns and warn you before you actually exceed the budget.

questions.question: In a high-security environment, which combination provides the STRONGEST authentication?

explanation.correct: Multiple hardware-based factors (Hardware Token + Security Key) provide the strongest protection - both are phishing-resistant and air-gapped.
explanation.why: While 'B' isn't standard (typically you'd use one MFA type), the question asks for strongest. Hardware factors beat virtual/SMS.

questions.question: What happens to your AWS Budget if you delete all resources and have zero spending for a month?

options.text: You won't receive any alerts that month
The budget remains active and continues monitoring
AWS stops charging for the budget

explanation.correct: Budgets remain active regardless of spending levels. They continue monitoring and will alert if spending resumes.
explanation.why: Budgets are persistent until you manually delete them. Zero spending means zero alerts, but the budget keeps watching.

questions.question: A company has MFA enabled but an employee's laptop was compromised by malware. Can the attacker access AWS?

options.text: Yes, if the laptop had saved credentials
No, MFA prevents all access from compromised devices
Possibly, if malware captures both password AND MFA codes in real-time
Only if the employee used SMS-based MFA

explanation.correct: Sophisticated malware could capture both password entry and MFA codes as they're entered, then use them before codes expire (30-second window).
explanation.why: MFA significantly reduces risk but isn't 100% bulletproof against advanced real-time malware. This is why hardware keys (phishing-resistant) are best for high-security scenarios.

questions.question: You want to track both EC2 costs and S3 costs separately with different budget limits. How many budgets do you need?

options.text: 2 budgets (one for EC2, one for S3)

explanation.correct: Each budget can track one spending limit. To have different limits for EC2 and S3, you need separate budgets with service filters.
explanation.why: Budget #1: Filter for EC2 only, limit $50. Budget #2: Filter for S3 only, limit $20. Each monitors its specific service.

questions.question: What is the BEST strategy for a company with 10 AWS accounts?

options.text: MFA on Root only in primary account
MFA on Root in all 10 accounts + Budgets in each
Use AWS Organizations with consolidated billing and budgets
MFA not needed with multiple accounts

explanation.correct: AWS Organizations allows centralized management with consolidated billing and organization-level budgets, plus MFA enforcement policies.
explanation.why: Managing 10 separate accounts is inefficient. Organizations provides centralized security, billing, and budget management across all accounts.
